meta.title: Adventure Paths & Bosses
meta.description: How every run's adventure path is generated: the 16 room types and the rules that decide which ones appear, and the boss ladder — eight gyms, four Elite Four, the Champion, and one final step we'll leave you to discover. The path generator is identical between Vanilla and EX — what differs is which species, trainers and legendaries can show up in the rooms.

prose.heading: What a run looks like
prose.text: A run is a chain of path segments, one per badge step, re-rolled after each boss. Read left to right: Hub, rooms, split, boss. Classic: 5 steps (3 rooms, split, boss); Fast Path: 6 — 4 when routes are hidden, 5 at the Champion stage; Gauntlet: 7 on badge 0, then 2 after the first badge (boss right after the split). The layout is seeded from your run seed and badge count, so the same badge can still roll a different trail.

prose.heading: Climbing the ladder
prose.text: The boss you face is fixed by your badge count: the room at the end of the path is always the next one on the ladder — you can't skip ahead or fight a boss out of order. Past the Champion there is one more step, best left for you to find in-game.

prose.heading: Reading the rooms
prose.text: Every room announces itself before you enter: 'It's a Mighty Trainer!', 'It's a Pokémon of Legends!', 'It's a Dark Deal…?', 'It's a Mysterious Shrine.' Only the boss at the end is mandatory — the run only advances once you've dealt with it.

records.name: Route
records.description: The default room. Every column of the path starts out as a route and only becomes a special encounter if one is placed. Routes come in three sub-types — Calm, Average and Tough. The sub-type does not shift the wild Pokémon's level range (wild levels scale with your own level) — it tunes what the route offers: trainer mon levels (Calm at the tier's start level, Average at the midpoint between the start level and your level, Tough at your level minus 5), encounter counts (grass 5/3/2, water 2/1/1), trainer spawn chance (20 points less on Calm), item drop chance (65/80/95) with rarity adjusted (−1/0/+1), and themed-weather chance (5/25/45). The three-type wild table itself is defined per route; see the Routes page.

placement.note: the default room — special encounters replace routes

records.name: Mighty Trainer (Boss)
records.description: The boss room, always placed at the very end of the path (preview: 'It's a Mighty Trainer!'). It is the only mandatory room: which boss appears depends on your badge count — a Gym Leader, Elite Four member, the Champion — or, at the very top of the ladder, a final battle we won't spoil. After the boss, a new path is generated for the next ladder step.
records.source: include/constants/rogue.h @vanilla L257 / @origin/expansion L257 (ADVPATH_ROOM_BOSS); src/rogue_adventurepaths.c @vanilla L648-649 (boss placed at path end), L1860-1881 (SetBossRoomWarp maps difficulty to the boss room) (identical @origin/expansion)

records.name: Rest Stop
records.description: An outdoor respite area with four sub-types: Full (healing), Mart (item shop), Battle Prep (tutors) and Day Care. Resting doesn't pause the run — the clock still advances 60 in-game minutes for every map you enter — and a rest stop is a room like any other: it can be the one where your run's pre-rolled rival battle appears, with the hidden rival NPC, parked at the room's north exit, revealed inside the room you enter. Rival encounters only happen inside rooms — never on the path overview map, which has no object events at all — and never in Gauntlet runs. The generator strongly wants at least one (weight 100 when none is on the current path, 20 when one is already placed, a low weight of 5 for two or three, and 1 once four are). In the badge-0 Gauntlet path, the route column closest to the boss is replaced with a Full Rest Stop — so that path ends with a free full heal right before the boss battle.

placement.note: weight, by rest stops already on the path

records.name: Legendary Encounter
records.description: A lone legendary roamer battle (preview: 'It's a Pokémon of Legends!'). A run is assigned up to three legendary slots — a Roamer legendary at badges 1–5, a Minor legendary at badges 3–5, and the Box legendary at badges 7–8, with collisions shifted apart — and each slot is placed on its assigned badge's path with the highest weight of any room (200), at most one per path, so a run can meet up to three legendaries. In Fast Path, the assigned badge snaps down to the even-numbered column — hidden-route segments don't host legendaries at all. In EX the pool of legendaries grows with each generation; in Vanilla it is the Gen 1–3 set.

placement.note: placed on its assigned badge · one per path

records.name: Team Hideout
records.description: A multi-battle raid on a villain team's hideout (preview: 'It's a Team Hideout!'). Two per run in Classic and Fast Path (Early + Pre-Legend) — Gauntlet runs have none — at weight 50, one per path: the Early hideout lands on a random badge between 2 and 4 — re-rolled until it misses the Roamer and Minor legendary badges (the Box legendary's badge is not checked) — and the Pre-Legend hideout lands on the same badge as the Box legendary. In Fast Path the Early badge snaps to an even-numbered column. Each villain team has its own pair of hideout maps, one per encounter: Rocket (Kanto and Johto) raid the Rocket Hideout then the Silph Co, Aqua raid the Aqua Hideout then the Seafloor Cavern, and Magma raid Mt. Chimney then the Magma Hideout. The raiding team is drawn from the teams of your enabled regions, and EX adds three more, each with dedicated maps: Galactic (Lake Valor / Galactic HQ), Plasma (Charge Stone Cave / Dragon Spiral Tower) and Flare (Poké Ball Factory / Lysandre Labs) — Neo Plasma has map entries but is disabled while it is being completed.

placement.note: placed on its assigned badge · one per path

records.name: Honey Tree
records.description: A honey tree habitat with a wild encounter and a honey reward (preview: 'It's a Honey Tree Habitat!'). From badge 1 up it passes a 60% roll on each path; when it does, the generator cycles its placement weight by badge parity (15 on odd badges, 1 on even) and places at most one per path — so picking up several honey trees across a run's segments is normal.
records.source: include/constants/rogue.h @vanilla L247 / @origin/expansion L247 (ADVPATH_ROOM_HONEY_TREE); src/rogue_adventurepaths.c @vanilla L390-403 (honey tree weight, one per path), L732-733 (60% roll, badge ≥ 1) (identical @origin/expansion)

placement.note: after a 60% path roll · badge 1+ · one per path

records.name: Dark Deal
records.description: A graveyard encounter (preview: 'It's a Dark Deal…?'). A devil salesman offers a choice of three Charms — take one, and he 'afflicts' you with a random Curse as the price. It can only be offered from badge 3 up (earlier badges are Game Show territory), needs a 25% roll for the path and is skipped on badges that are multiples of three; from badge 6 up it's the only special encounter offered. Gauntlet runs ignore the multiple-of-three skip but still need the same 25% roll. Placement weight cycles with badge parity (15 on odd, 1 on even), and at most one per path (per badge step).

placement.note: after a 25% path roll · badge 3+ · skip badges divisible by 3

records.name: Professor Birch's Lab
records.description: A lab encounter (preview: 'It's a Pokémon Lab.'). Birch has caught up to three Pokémon you released during the run and will let you take one back; the others wait at the lab, sometimes holding an item — occasionally a Curse. It can only be offered from badge 3 up, needs a 25% roll for the path and is skipped on badges where (badge mod 3) is 1; the placement weight is 20 on even-numbered badges and 1 on odd-numbered ones (of the seven badges it can appear on, only three get the high weight), at most one per path, and never in Gauntlet.

placement.note: after a 25% path roll · badge 3+ · skip if badge mod 3 = 1 · never in Gauntlet

records.name: Mysterious Shrine
records.description: A shrine encounter (preview: 'It's a Mysterious Shrine.'). The shrine keeper will gift you the Sacred Ash — a one-time 'whole party revives and teleports to safety' insurance — but carrying it requires taking the Capacity Curse, which reduces your maximum party size by one. The generator strongly wants it when it appears (weight 100), on one pre-rolled badge per run — unlike most of the other special rooms, whose cap of one is per path — or always in Gauntlet.

placement.note: the run's pre-rolled badge · always in Gauntlet

records.name: Game Show
records.description: Mr. Randoman's Game Show (preview: 'It's a… Game Show?'). Pick a Game of Skill or a Game of Luck, play up to six rounds, and cash out at any time — every round you complete adds another item to your haul, all or nothing. Interact with the prize shelf or counter while a prize slot is still unearned — no item currently won — and Randoman replies with a note, 'Cheaters never prosper ke ke ke', followed by a wild Electrode battle that cannot be caught. It's only offered on badges 0–5 (50% roll per path; from badge 3 up it shares the slot with the Dark Deal) and never in Gauntlet.
records.source: data/maps/Rogue_Encounter_GameShow/scripts.pory @vanilla L56-142 (host, categories, game selection), L158-175 (cheating triggers the Electrode battle) (identical @origin/expansion); src/rogue_adventurepaths.c @vanilla L428-435 (Game Show weight, one per path), L784-825 (50% roll, badges 0–2 only, 3–5 shared with Dark Deal, none from badge 6, gauntlet exclusion) (identical @origin/expansion)

records.name: Catching Contest
records.description: A catch practice arena (preview: 'It's a Catching Contest.'). The host announces a species type and a base stat, then 10–29 non-legendary Pokémon of that type spawn on a fixed interval; your party is stashed away and you are given exactly 3 contest Poké Balls. You win if the mon you keep has a base value in the announced stat at least equal to the highest among the spawned ones — the reward is a fixed ¥5,000, ¥10,000 or ¥15,000 by difficulty — and you keep the catch regardless (releasing a party mon to make room if needed). Rolled into a third of paths (33%), at most one per path.
records.source: include/constants/rogue.h @vanilla L252 / @origin/expansion L252 (ADVPATH_ROOM_CATCHING_CONTEST); src/rogue_adventurepaths.c @vanilla L446-451 (contest weight), L768-770 (33% roll) (identical @origin/expansion); src/rogue_followmon.c @vanilla L1134-1139 (fixed 120-tick spawn interval during contests) (identical @origin/expansion)

records.name: Mysterious Sign
records.description: A sign maker's workshop (preview: 'It's a Mysterious Sign.'). The maker produces the signs inside the gyms, and will give you advance intel on the next Gym Leader: its specialisation type for free, the leader's lead Pokémon for ¥4,000, or their strongest Pokémon for ¥2,500 (once paid, each answer sticks). Only offered before the Elite Four (40% roll per path, below Elite Four only).
records.source: data/maps/Rogue_Encounter_Sign/scripts.pory @vanilla L21-39 (free type hint), L77-169 (¥4,000 lead / ¥2,500 strongest Pokémon reveals, paid-once flags) (identical @origin/expansion); src/rogue_adventurepaths.c @vanilla L428-435 (Sign weight, one per path), L736-737 (only below Elite Four difficulty, 40% roll) (identical @origin/expansion)

records.name: Battle Simulator
records.description: A wager battle (preview: 'It's a Battle Simulator.'). Each side fields 3 random Lv50 Pokémon and you pick the stake before the fight: money (win ¥5,000 / ¥10,000 / ¥15,000 by difficulty; lose = half your money), IVs (nominate a party mon — win raises all six of its IVs by 10, capped at 31; lose lowers them by 10 — a legitimate way to invest in a mon's IVs), or items (win = a valuable item stack worth about 10× a Rare Candy's price; lose = up to 5 stacks removed to match that value). One battle per visit; from badge 1 up, 50/50 against the Battle Tower, at most one per path.
records.source: include/constants/rogue.h @vanilla L254 / @origin/expansion L254 (ADVPATH_ROOM_BATTLE_SIM); src/rogue_adventurepaths.c @vanilla L438-444 (Battle Sim weight, one per path), L772-779 (50/50 vs Battle Tower) (identical @origin/expansion)

records.name: Battle Tower
records.description: A frontier-style battle (preview: 'It's a Battle Tower.'). Another randomised trainer battle, but with a random weather condition set for the fight — Sunny, Sandstorm, Drought, Downpour, Falling Leaves, Rain and Thunderstorm, Psychic Fog, Snow or Misty Fog, with no weather as a possible roll — never rolled on Easy. From badge 1 up, at most one per path (the 50/50 alternative to the Battle Simulator).
records.source: include/constants/rogue.h @vanilla L255 / @origin/expansion L255 (ADVPATH_ROOM_BATTLE_TOWER); src/rogue_controller.c @vanilla L6025-6049 (9-condition weather list, rolled per entry, skipped on Easy) / @origin/expansion L6016-6040

records.name: Wild Den
records.description: A habitat of one specific species (preview: 'It's a {species} Habitat of a Trained Pokémon!'). A den of trained Pokémon of a single species for you to fight or catch. Dens can appear on any path: every remaining route column rolls to become one, with a chance by tier — 90% at the Champion and beyond, 60% for the Elite Four, 40% on badges 1–7, 5% on badge 0 — falling a few points with each den placed, while a minimum number of regular routes is always kept (1 at the Champion and beyond, 2 for the Elite Four, 3 on badges 0–7). On Fast Path hidden-route steps, every remaining route of that segment becomes a den — that segment is den-hopping, not the whole run.
records.source: include/constants/rogue.h @vanilla L246 / @origin/expansion L246 (ADVPATH_ROOM_WILD_DEN); src/rogue_adventurepaths.c @vanilla L869-880 (fast path with hidden routes: every remaining route of the path becomes a den) (identical @origin/expansion); data/maps/Rogue_AdventurePaths/scripts.pory @vanilla L48-49 (den preview text) (identical @origin/expansion)

placement.note: each remaining route rolls · chance falls off per den

records.name: Gap (Empty Tile)
records.description: A gap in the path — a route column that was blanked out so the trail has open space. The chance of a gap grows with the difficulty (5% early, 20% for the Elite Four, 30% for the Champion and beyond, falling off a few points per gap), and never happens on the very first badge or in Gauntlet.
records.source: include/constants/rogue.h @vanilla L240 / @origin/expansion L240 (ADVPATH_ROOM_NONE); src/rogue_adventurepaths.c @vanilla L678-721 (gap chance by difficulty), zero on badge 0 and gauntlet) (identical @origin/expansion)

placement.note: chance falls off per gap · never badge 0 or Gauntlet

records.name: Miniboss (Reserved)
records.description: A 'Strong Trainer' room type that is fully wired (map, reward flow — a Charm plus two Pokémon — and preview text) but is not currently placed by the path generator; the code even marks it 'unused'. It exists so a future update can drop minibosses onto paths.

placement.note: fully wired, unused by the generator

records.name: Gym Leaders (Badges 0–7)
records.description: The first eight bosses on the ladder, one per badge, fought in the generic gym boss room. Each leader's team scales with the difficulty setting and is assembled from the enabled trainer pool (in EX you can include Sinnoh through Paldea leaders).
records.source: include/constants/rogue.h @vanilla L377-383 / @origin/expansion L377-383 (14 = 8 gyms + 4 elite + 2 champion, ROGUE_ELITE_START_DIFFICULTY 8); src/rogue_adventurepaths.c @vanilla L1876-1880 (badge < 8 uses the generic gym boss room) (identical @origin/expansion)

records.name: Elite Four (Badges 8–11)
records.description: Badges 8 through 11 are Elite Four battles. The four members are drawn from a named pool — the regional Elite Four of your enabled regions plus the Rogue glitch-team elites (Kate, Erma, Raven and friends) — and the generator picks each elite's preferred arena map, so the four members get distinct battlegrounds rather than reusing the gym room. Some elites carry a shiny ace Pokémon that differs between versions (see the Versions page).
records.source: include/constants/rogue.h @vanilla L381 / @origin/expansion L381 (ROGUE_ELITE_START_DIFFICULTY 8); src/rogue_adventurepaths.c @vanilla L1872-1875 (elite members use their preferred map) (identical @origin/expansion); src/data/rogue/trainers/rogue.json @vanilla L666, L790, L1121 (glitch elites KATE/ERMA/RAVEN with shiny aces), all regional trainer files (BOSS_ANY_ELITE pool) (identical @origin/expansion)

records.name: Champion (Badge 12)
records.description: Badge 12 is the Champion, fought in the dedicated Champion arena. Your opponent is Randoman — the same contest judge who hosts the Game Show — and his team is a six-Pokémon party the generator assembles with a soft bias toward unique types: a candidate whose type is already in the team simply gets no extra weight, so duplicate types can still appear. It's the last battle you'd expect — what comes after is best left to the game.
records.source: src/data/rogue/trainers/rogue.json @vanilla L1511-1543 (RANDOMAN champ entry: 6-mon team, unique-type weight script, FINAL_BOSS_POKEBALL) (identical @origin/expansion); src/rogue_query_script.c @vanilla L322-327 (HasUniqueTypeInTeam), L409-415 (IncFavour: +1 weight only) (identical @origin/expansion); include/constants/rogue.h @vanilla L380 / @origin/expansion L380 (ROGUE_CHAMP_START_DIFFICULTY 12); src/rogue_adventurepaths.c @vanilla L1867-1871 (badge 12 uses the Champion boss room) (identical @origin/expansion)

records.name: Final Battle (Badge 13)
records.description: Badge 13 — the top of the ladder. Who you face here, and what the fight throws at you, are left as a surprise; the citation below points at the code if you'd rather peek.

records.name: Victory Lap
records.description: After the top of the ladder, a run can continue in an endless trainer-battle mode. What exactly that is best left for you to discover in-game.
